questions.prompt: Before integrating \(\frac{x^3+2}{x+1}\), should polynomial division be used?
questions.answer: Yes. The numerator has degree \(3\), and the denominator has degree \(1\). Since \(3\ge1\), the rational function is improper. Divide first so it becomes a polynomial plus a proper fraction.

questions.prompt: In polynomial division, what condition must the remainder \(R(x)\) satisfy when dividing by \(Q(x)\)?
questions.answer:
The remainder must have smaller degree than the divisor:
\[\deg R<\deg Q.\]
That is what makes \(\frac{R(x)}{Q(x)}\) a proper rational function.

Divide leading terms: \(x^2\div x=x\).
Multiply and subtract:
\[(x^2+5x+6)-(x^2+2x)=3x+6.\]
Next \(3x\div x=3\).
Multiply and subtract:
\[(3x+6)-(3x+6)=0.\]
So
\[\boxed{x^2+5x+6=(x+2)(x+3)}.\]

questions.prompt: Write \(\frac{x^2+1}{x-1}\) as a polynomial plus a proper fraction.
questions.answer:
Divide \(x^2+1\) by \(x-1\).
First \(x^2\div x=x\), giving subtraction \((x^2+1)-(x^2-x)=x+1\).
Next \(x\div x=1\), giving subtraction \((x+1)-(x-1)=2\).
Thus
\[x^2+1=(x-1)(x+1)+2.\]
Therefore
\[\boxed{\frac{x^2+1}{x-1}=x+1+\frac{2}{x-1}}.\]

questions.prompt: Evaluate \(\int \frac{x^2+1}{x}\,dx\).
questions.answer:
First divide term by term:
\[\frac{x^2+1}{x}=x+\frac{1}{x}.\]
Then integrate:
\[\int\left(x+\frac1x\right)dx=\frac{x^2}{2}+\ln|x|+C.\]
So
\[\boxed{\frac{x^2}{2}+\ln|x|+C}.\]

questions.prompt: Evaluate \(\int \frac{x^2-4x+5}{x-2}\,dx\).
questions.answer:
Divide \(x^2-4x+5\) by \(x-2\).
The quotient is \(x-2\) because
\[(x-2)(x-2)=x^2-4x+4.\]
The remainder is \(1\). Thus
\[\frac{x^2-4x+5}{x-2}=x-2+\frac{1}{x-2}.\]
Integrate:
\[\boxed{\frac{x^2}{2}-2x+\ln|x-2|+C}.\]

First \(2x^3\div x=2x^2\). Subtract \(2x^3+4x^2\) to get \(-x^2-x+4\).
Next \(-x^2\div x=-x\). Subtract \(-x^2-2x\) to get \(x+4\).
Next \(x\div x=1\). Subtract \(x+2\) to get \(2\).
So
\[\boxed{2x^3+3x^2-x+4=(x+2)(2x^2-x+1)+2}.\]

questions.prompt: Evaluate \(\int \frac{x^3+x}{x^2+1}\,dx\).
questions.answer:
Since
\[x^3+x=x(x^2+1),\]
the division has quotient \(x\) and remainder \(0\). Thus
\[\frac{x^3+x}{x^2+1}=x.\]
Therefore
\[\int \frac{x^3+x}{x^2+1}\,dx=\int x\,dx=\boxed{\frac{x^2}{2}+C}.\]

questions.prompt: Evaluate \(\int \frac{x^3+2x^2+x+5}{x+1}\,dx\).
questions.answer:
Divide by \(x+1\).
\(x^3\div x=x^2\); subtract \(x^3+x^2\) to get \(x^2+x+5\).
\(x^2\div x=x\); subtract \(x^2+x\) to get \(5\).
Thus
\[\frac{x^3+2x^2+x+5}{x+1}=x^2+x+\frac{5}{x+1}.\]
Integrate:
\[\boxed{\frac{x^3}{3}+\frac{x^2}{2}+5\ln|x+1|+C}.\]

questions.prompt: Evaluate \(\int \frac{2x^3-x^2+4}{x^2+1}\,dx\).
questions.answer:
Divide \(2x^3-x^2+0x+4\) by \(x^2+1\).
First term: \(2x^3\div x^2=2x\). Subtract \(2x^3+2x\), leaving \(-x^2-2x+4\).
Next term: \(-x^2\div x^2=-1\). Subtract \(-x^2-1\), leaving \(-2x+5\).
So
\[\frac{2x^3-x^2+4}{x^2+1}=2x-1+\frac{-2x+5}{x^2+1}.\]
Integrate:
\[\int(2x-1)dx-\int\frac{2x}{x^2+1}dx+5\int\frac{dx}{x^2+1}.\]
Therefore
\[\boxed{x^2-x-\ln(x^2+1)+5\arctan x+C}.\]

questions.prompt: Evaluate \(\int \frac{x^4+1}{x^2+1}\,dx\).
questions.answer:
Divide \(x^4+0x^3+0x^2+0x+1\) by \(x^2+1\).
\(x^4\div x^2=x^2\). Subtract \(x^4+x^2\), leaving \(-x^2+1\).
\(-x^2\div x^2=-1\). Subtract \(-x^2-1\), leaving \(2\).
Thus
\[\frac{x^4+1}{x^2+1}=x^2-1+\frac{2}{x^2+1}.\]
Integrate:
\[\boxed{\frac{x^3}{3}-x+2\arctan x+C}.\]
The remainder has degree \(0<2\), so division is complete.

questions.prompt: A student writes \(\frac{x^3-1}{x-1}=x^2+1\). Explain the error and give the correct quotient.
questions.answer:
The factorisation is
\[x^3-1=(x-1)(x^2+x+1),\]
not \((x-1)(x^2+1)\).
Checking the student's answer:
\[(x-1)(x^2+1)=x^3-x^2+x-1,\]
which is not \(x^3-1\).
Therefore
\[\boxed{\frac{x^3-1}{x-1}=x^2+x+1}\]
for \(x\ne1\).

questions.prompt: Evaluate \(\int \frac{x^4-3x^2+2x+7}{x^2-1}\,dx\).
Evaluate \(\int \frac{3x^4+x^3+2x+1}{x^2+x}\,dx\).
questions.answer:
Use denominator \(x^2+x\). Divide:
\(3x^4\div x^2=3x^2\). Subtract \(3x^4+3x^3\), leaving \(-2x^3+0x^2+2x+1\).
\(-2x^3\div x^2=-2x\). Subtract \(-2x^3-2x^2\), leaving \(2x^2+2x+1\).
\(2x^2\div x^2=2\). Subtract \(2x^2+2x\), leaving \(1\).
Thus
\[\frac{3x^4+x^3+2x+1}{x^2+x}=3x^2-2x+2+\frac{1}{x(x+1)}.\]
And
\[\frac{1}{x(x+1)}=\frac{1}{x}-\frac{1}{x+1}.\]
Integrate:
\[\boxed{x^3-x^2+2x+\ln|x|-\ln|x+1|+C}.\]

questions.prompt: Find \(a\) so that dividing \(x^3+ax+4\) by \(x-2\) leaves remainder \(0\), then write the quotient.
questions.answer:
By the remainder theorem, the remainder on division by \(x-2\) is the value at \(x=2\):
\[2^3+a(2)+4=12+2a.\]
Set this equal to zero:
\[12+2a=0\Rightarrow a=-6.\]
Now divide \(x^3-6x+4\) by \(x-2\). The quotient is
\[x^2+2x-2\]
because
\[(x-2)(x^2+2x-2)=x^3-6x+4.\]
So
\[\boxed{a=-6,\quad \text{quotient }x^2+2x-2}.\]

questions.prompt: Find \(k\) so that \(\frac{x^3+kx+1}{x^2+1}\) has remainder \(1\) after division, then integrate the rational function.
questions.answer:
Divide \(x^3+kx+1\) by \(x^2+1\). The first quotient term is \(x\), giving product \(x^3+x\).
The remainder is
\[(x^3+kx+1)-(x^3+x)=(k-1)x+1.\]
For the remainder to be exactly \(1\), need \(k-1=0\), so \(k=1\).
Then
\[\frac{x^3+x+1}{x^2+1}=x+\frac{1}{x^2+1}.\]
Integrate:
\[\boxed{k=1,\quad \int \frac{x^3+x+1}{x^2+1}\,dx=\frac{x^2}{2}+\arctan x+C}.\]

questions.prompt: For what values of \(m\) and \(n\) is \(x^3+mx+n\) exactly divisible by \(x^2-1\)?
questions.answer:
Exact divisibility by \(x^2-1=(x-1)(x+1)\) means the polynomial is zero at both \(x=1\) and \(x=-1\).
At \(x=1\):
\[1+m+n=0.\]
At \(x=-1\):
\[-1-m+n=0.\]
Add the equations:
\[2n=0\Rightarrow n=0.\]
Then \(1+m=0\), so \(m=-1\).
Therefore
\[\boxed{m=-1,\quad n=0}.\]

questions.prompt: A student divides \(x^4+2x^2+3\) by \(x^2+1\) and stops at \(x^2+2\) with remainder \(3\). Diagnose the error and give the correct decomposition.
questions.answer:
Check the student's result:
\[(x^2+1)(x^2+2)+3=x^4+3x^2+5,\]
which is not \(x^4+2x^2+3\).
Correct division: \(x^4\div x^2=x^2\). Subtract \(x^4+x^2\), leaving \(x^2+3\).
Next \(x^2\div x^2=1\). Subtract \(x^2+1\), leaving \(2\).
So
\[\boxed{\frac{x^4+2x^2+3}{x^2+1}=x^2+1+\frac{2}{x^2+1}}.\]

questions.prompt: Prove that if \(\deg P\ge \deg Q\) and \(Q\ne0\), polynomial division writes \(\frac{P(x)}{Q(x)}=S(x)+\frac{R(x)}{Q(x)}\) with \(\deg R<\deg Q\).
questions.answer:
Polynomial division gives polynomials \(S(x)\) and \(R(x)\) such that
\[P(x)=Q(x)S(x)+R(x),\]
where either \(R(x)=0\) or \(\deg R<\deg Q\).
Divide both sides by \(Q(x)\):
\[\frac{P(x)}{Q(x)}=\frac{Q(x)S(x)}{Q(x)}+\frac{R(x)}{Q(x)}.\]
Since \(Q(x)\ne0\) on the domain of the rational function, this simplifies to
\[\frac{P(x)}{Q(x)}=S(x)+\frac{R(x)}{Q(x)}.\]
The degree condition makes the remaining fraction proper.

questions.prompt: Evaluate \(\int \frac{x^5-x^4+x^2+1}{x^2+1}\,dx\), showing the division and the remaining standard integrals.
questions.answer:
Divide by \(x^2+1\).
\(x^5\div x^2=x^3\). Subtract \(x^5+x^3\), leaving \(-x^4-x^3+x^2+1\).
\(-x^4\div x^2=-x^2\). Subtract \(-x^4-x^2\), leaving \(-x^3+2x^2+1\).
\(-x^3\div x^2=-x\). Subtract \(-x^3-x\), leaving \(2x^2+x+1\).
\(2x^2\div x^2=2\). Subtract \(2x^2+2\), leaving \(x-1\).
Thus
\[\frac{x^5-x^4+x^2+1}{x^2+1}=x^3-x^2-x+2+\frac{x-1}{x^2+1}.\]
Integrate:
\[\int(x^3-x^2-x+2)dx+\int\frac{x}{x^2+1}dx-\int\frac{dx}{x^2+1}.\]
Therefore
\[\boxed{\frac{x^4}{4}-\frac{x^3}{3}-\frac{x^2}{2}+2x+\frac12\ln(x^2+1)-\arctan x+C}.\]
